These entities may be responsible for identifying the transmission need and supporting the transmission planning region in the identification and cost allocation of transmission solutions to meet that need. 3.2 Case Study Summaries The following sections provide details on each case study, highlighting the project details and cost allocation outcomes. More information on each case study is provided in Appendix C. 3.2.1 MISO Multi-Value Project Planning Portfolio The MISO Multi-Value Project (MVP) portfolio demonstrates the application of a portfolio approach (i.e., multi-project/driver) to project planning and cost allocation and a balance of rigorous technical analysis for project benefits evaluation combined with a simple method for cost allocation. The initial MVP portfolio includes 17 projects identified through MISO’s 2011 Transmission Expansion Plan (MTEP 11).9 These projects were initially championed by the governors of seven member states with growing concerns over the “crisis” generation developers face because of a lack of transmission for interconnection (MISO 2011; Boyd and Garvey 2021). Various regional initiatives organized by the states assisted MISO in developing cost allocation proposals as well as model inputs and assumptions that were used for the MTEP 11 (MISO 2011). Figure 5 shows the projects included in the 2011 MVP portfolio. The projects consist of high- voltage alternating current (AC) transmission upgrades at 345 kV or higher and are distributed throughout MISO’s Midwestern planning footprint.10 As of March 2025, all but 1 of the 17 proposed projects have been constructed and are in service (MISO 2025). 9 More information about subsequent MISO MVP portfolios is available at: https://www.misoenergy.org/planning/multi-value-projects-mvps/#t=10&p=0&s=Updated&sd=desc. 10 At the time, this only included what is today the MISO Midwest subregion. 13 This report is available at no cost from the National Laboratory of the Rockies at www.nlr.gov/publications. Source: (MISO 2014) MVPs are large, regional projects that provide reliability, economic, and public policy benefits throughout the MISO footprint or subregion.11 MISO quantified multiple economic benefit metrics for the portfolio, including production cost savings, reduced transmission losses, and deferred capacity and transmission investments. These benefits were calculated for individual cost allocation zones, which align with utility and (roughly) state boundaries, to allow state regulators and members to assess the benefits attributed to the zone covering their state.
